_meta.semantics: covers_syllabus_refs is an index of the objectives a stage is principally associated with; coverage is claimed only through _syllabus_items + covers_items, and only as far as coverage_check.py confirms.

_items_source.document: AQA GCSE Economics (8136) specification: subject content Topics 1-11 (3.1 How markets work; 3.2 How the economy works)
_items_source.version: Specification for first teaching from September 2017, the current version linked from aqa.org.uk/8136, itemised 2026-09-27
_items_source.numbering: AQA numbers this specification's subject content by topic and sub-topic (e.g. 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 within Topic 1), not with a further leading section digit as some other AQA GCSE specifications use. This course keeps AQA's own topic.subtopic codes (1.1-1.3, 2.1-2.3, 3.1-3.6, 4.1-4.3, 5.1-5.4, 6.1-6.2, 7.1-7.2, 8.1-8.6, 9.1-9.4, 10.1-10.4, 11.1-11.2) exactly as AQA presents them across the 11 topics, itemised from AQA's published subject-content pages and specification PDF.

_syllabus_items.title: Economic activity: needs and wants, the central purpose of economic activity, the key economic decisions, the main economic groups
The factors of production
Making choices: the basic economic problem, costs and benefits of economic choices including opportunity cost
Markets and the allocation of resources, including factor and product markets
Economic sectors: primary, secondary and tertiary; goods and services
Specialisation, division of labour and exchange: benefits and costs
Demand for goods and services: factors, causes of changes, and the demand curve
Supply of goods and services: factors, causes of changes, and the supply curve
Equilibrium price
Intermarket relationships: complements and substitutes
Price elasticity of demand: meaning, factors and measurement
Price elasticity of supply: meaning, factors and measurement
The importance of cost, revenue and profit for producers, including business objectives and moral/ethical considerations
